picks.title: 'Beyond human intuition': AI designs chip components 500 times smaller than what engineers could ever imagine
picks.excerpt: Three new AI-designed chip components measure just a few micrometers and take geometries no human engineer had proposed. The researchers frame the designs as literally beyond human intuition rather than incremental optimizations of known layouts.
picks.rationale: Generative design crossing from styling into physics-constrained hardware: the shapes are unrecognizable, they work, and no designer would have drawn them.

picks.title: Most AI medical devices cleared for use were not tested on patient outcomes
picks.excerpt: Of 1,357 AI-based medical devices the FDA has authorized for patient care, only three were tested on whether they actually improve patients' health, a new analysis finds. A hard number on the evidence gap between AI clearance and AI benefit.
picks.rationale: Three out of 1,357 is the most quotable number in AI evaluation this week — clearance is not evidence, and anyone designing or trusting AI health features should hold that distinction.

picks.title: AI's recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
picks.excerpt: New evaluations suggest AI agents are not yet creative enough to carry out genuinely innovative, open-ended AI research — undercutting the assumption that models will soon bootstrap their own progress. A measured empirical check on the fastest-moving claim in the field.
picks.rationale: The 'AI improves itself' premise finally gets measured instead of asserted, and it fails at the originality step — a calibration point for every roadmap built on that assumption.

picks.title: Operation Blue Skies: Reducing aviation climate impact with AI
picks.excerpt: Google and the UK are running Operation Blue Skies, an airspace-scale trial of AI-powered contrail avoidance — rerouting flights around the atmospheric conditions that make persistent contrails. It moves contrail forecasting from paper study to live operational science.
picks.rationale: A climate model that leaves the paper and starts steering real aircraft — the rare case where an AI prediction is wired directly into an operational system at national scale.

picks.title: Experiment shows how AI discoveries can shape human cultural evolution
picks.excerpt: In a multigenerational lab task, Max Planck researchers found humans almost never discovered a strategy that required short-term losses for later gains — but groups seeded with AI agents adopted it and passed it down across generations. The study maps the conditions under which machine-found solutions actually enter human culture.
picks.rationale: An experimental answer to whether machine-found ideas actually stick in human practice: they do, but mainly when the payoff is delayed enough that people never found them alone.
